story: To avenge his brother, Hiranyakashipu performed severe penance and won a boon from Brahma: he could not be killed by man or animal, indoors or outdoors, by day or night, on the ground or in the sky, by any weapon. Then he declared himself God and tried to kill his son Prahlada for worshipping Vishnu.
belief: He is remembered as the ultimate image of arrogance. His end shows that no clever loophole protects anyone from the results of their actions.
turns: He demanded to be worshipped and tried to kill his own child. Vishnu, as Narasimha, half man and half lion, killed him at dusk, on a doorstep, on his lap, with his claws.
facts: His brother Hiranyaksha was killed by Vishnu's boar avatar, Varaha.
Holika Dahan, the bonfire before Holi, comes from his sister's attempt to burn Prahlada.
He and his brother were once Jaya and Vijaya, Vishnu's gatekeepers, cursed to be born as asuras.
